title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while in autonomous mode. The vehicle did not brake or slow down as it approached the animal. This represents a failure in the perception or decision-making system to recognize and respond appropriately to a small moving object in its path.

The incident occurred during normal deployment in a residential neighborhood. It would have taken either better detection of small animals in the vehicle's sensor data, or a conservative braking response when an obstacle cannot be clearly identified, to prevent this outcome. Avride subsequently restricted service on certain streets and began testing improvements through simulation.

Whether the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign, as one resident claimed, is not established. Avride disputed this allegation and stated the vehicle stopped appropriately at all relevant signs.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting neighborhood residents to express concerns about self-driving car technology in their area. The incident gained attention after a resident posted about the incident on a neighborhood Facebook group, noting that the vehicle did not slow down or stop. The duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant, was known to residents, intensifying their reaction to the accident. Local residents have since placed the duck's eggs in an incubator.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time of the incident. The company also addressed a resident's claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, stating that it found no evidence supporting this and that the vehicle stopped appropriately at all relevant signs. In response to the incident, Avride has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. The company is now evaluating technological improvements through controlled simulations to prevent similar situations while maintaining safety performance.
